reason: Core claim holds; the stated hypothesis and falsifier prediction are wrong. Irreducibility over Q does not depend on ord_n(2). Capelli: T^n - alpha is irreducible over Q(alpha) unless alpha is an n-th power in Q(alpha). That happens only when E descends to F_2 (j in F_2). Data: an exhaustive scan of every odd trace a, plus supersingular a=0, at n=7,11,13 finds P(T^n) reducible only at a = +/- tr(tau^n) of the Koblitz curves (n=7: +/-13; n=11: +/-67; n=13: +/-181). Random samples of about 100 curves at n in {13,17,19,29,31,37,53,59,61,67,83} gave 0 reducible. For Koblitz, Psi is irreducible of degree 2(n-1) at every tested prime n, including the controls n=17 (ord 8) and n=31 (ord 5). It splits 6+6 only at n=7, because sqrt(-7) lies in Q(zeta_7). For supersingular a=0, (T^{2n}+2^n)/(T^2+2) is irreducible for all tested n. So ord_n(2)-blocks govern factorisation over F_2 (the subspace closure), not isogeny decomposition over F_2. Tate gives F_2-simplicity of R (generic E) and of the trace-zero A (Koblitz, n != 7). This adds no algorithmic leverage. Over F_{2^n}, R is isogenous to E^n, so the obstruction holds only over the base field F_2. The genus >= n-1 lower bound applies only to carrier curves defined over F_2 that have a nonzero map to R (resp. A). GHS-type curves over F_2 already satisfy it.
fix: Restate: for every odd prime n (not only those with 2 primitive), and every E/F_{2^n} with j(E) not in F_2, P_E(T^n) is irreducible over Q and R is F_2-simple. For Koblitz E, Psi is irreducible iff n != 7. At n=7, A ~ A1 x A2 with dim 3 each, an F_2-sub-abelian variety of dimension 3. Drop the 2-primitivity hypothesis and the ord_n(2)-block prediction. Classify as accounting/folklore with no wall bypass. B*D^2 is unaffected.
